text: A worker earning $2,400 for example, earns overtime pay and it goes much higher, compared to another worker who earns maybe $2,500 on the dot, looks more in terms of basic, but he does not earn any overtime pay because his sector, like administration, for example, that is all they have, hardly much overtime, but that is their base salary.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, is the guy earning $2,400 lower base with higher overtime pay, or the person earning $2,500 with no overtime pay, earning more?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In that sense, I think we also have to be very mindful that as we scope our schemes for lower-wage workers, we have to also be calibrated, at the same time also fair, to ensure that equity is maintained.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While I agree that many of our lower-wage workers do have the intention to earn more because some can do more overtime, for example.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But in reality, we also have to take into account all their incomes as a whole, because I think we have to also be fair in terms of how we support our lower-wage workers.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The first has to do with the scoring which currently gives 20 points default to firms smaller than 25 PMETs and I understand the premise behind that.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: The concern here of course is that we create an artificial ceiling for firms, just like it is for small firms in Italy, where they intentionally just stay below the medium-size threshold.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: My second question has to do with public data releases for the foundational criteria used to construct COMPASS.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: It would really help, I feel, if MOM will consider releasing data for sub-sectors to ensure firms and Singaporeans understand the reality of the given business environment.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: So, for example, for C1 in salary, we have data reported on gross monthly income from work at the median as well as the 20th percentile, but it will be useful to have it for the other sectors.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: Similarly, for C2 qualification, it would also be useful to understand the level of the highest qualification for our resident labour force and of those employed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Well, I was an entrepreneur and I founded a firm and subsequently, I have also in due funded a couple of startups.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think that as a growing firm, the first thing that you would assess, for the founder or the entrepreneur, is to assess the market and to know what are the rules that they will operate under.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Having said that, I think the length of time that we have given for everyone to try to adjust to the framework itself, I think it is a fairly long runway.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And the flexibility, the nimbleness, the responsiveness of the entrepreneur or the founder, is going to be quite paramount in ensuring that the firm will ultimately succeed.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And I am pretty sure that there are many private equity affiliate professionals here amongst us, I think who would probably agree and testify to that.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, on paper, it looks like as if it may cause a cliff effect, but I think in reality, given the nuanced approach, we believe that there will be enough time for people to adapt.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think there is still time for us to see when it comes to the implementation, how we can actually get a set of nuanced data for everyone to be able to access and also to understand.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, as we support them, as we use funding to support this group, the moment they get to a certain size, I think it is also the social compact and their responsibility to ensure that our Singaporean Core continues to be supported, to be brought along with them as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, it is not just about caring for our fellow Singaporeans, it is also about carrying them alongside with us as well.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope to get your support and your concurrence on this.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: One really builds on the point that the Minister spoke about with regard to the support to build a strong Singapore Core, which is I think the substance of this initiative to review the EP qualifying criteria, exemplified by COMPASS.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My question really picks off from a point I raised in the previous Budget, in the Committee of Supply debates last year about the Capability Transfer Programme.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just to enquire whether MOM considers in the renewal of the EPs going forward, a contribution of EP or their companies as a bonus criterion, if there has been a real transfer of skills to the Singapore Core?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Whether that could be a part of the system structure in renewing EP holders, getting more EP holders into Singapore in areas there clearly is a need?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Because I think this really will address a long-term bugbear that is a perception nonetheless that somehow the foreigners not playing their part in contributing to the growth of the Singapore Core.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If there is some data set, some matrix that can show that that is not the case and that actually there is a skills transfer that can be objectively assessed, I think this will be helpful for the programme.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Just another question, dealing with the EP framework.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I understand today there are probably about 160,000 to 170,000 EP holders.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: If the new scheme applied today, how many of these individuals would not actually be given their EP?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I am just wondering if the Minister has that information.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My final point is a very short one.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In his speech this morning, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad spoke about workers who earn less than $500.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think he made a clarification of the 20,000 figure but I did not catch what the new figure was.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I do not believe the Minister shared it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: But I would be grateful if the Senior Minister of State would share what that number actually is.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The short answer to your first point about whether we can consider firms' support in terms of the local training, the transfers of skillsets, I think as we evolve the framework, we are not closed off to this thinking.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: At some stage, we will be able to continue to tweak the framework.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Of course, we need to ensure that tweaking is not done in such a frequent manner that after a while, companies who want to look into investing into our country itself would think that we are having a series of moving goal posts.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, the consistency, the constancy of this framework must be preserved.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: However, at the fringe, anything that would strengthen it, to see how we can continue to improve our Singaporean Core, the transfer of skill sets, I think would be something that we can consider.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: If you talk about comparing with the numbers today, how many would pass the framework, I think it is difficult to compare.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Because in terms of, for instance, even at C1, notwithstanding the fact that we have a qualifying salary, even at C1, we measured according to the sector, what is the 65th percentile.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I think, just off the cuff, finance in general, already you can see that there are two separate categories.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, that is the number of new applicants applying to join and people leaving.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, this churn, when put through COMPASS, will more than adequately take care of what we intend to do over the horizon.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I hope that sort of gives you a picture of where we envisage we will move to.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: My clarification was basically to say that the Minister's speech quoting the 20,000 is the right number.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Because the way I mentioned it, the way I clarified, some might interpret it as the number was different or lower.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, I thought just to clarify that the Minister's speech was the correct number.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I am heartened to hear about the role of COMPASS to strengthen the complementarity of our foreign workforce.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, I would like to raise a few clarifications to the Minister.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I request that you could just to keep to one clarification and let others clarify.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: So, the clarification will be – how will it be administered?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: Will the companies do self-assessments on an automated system or will every application be assessed by an MOM officer?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: How do we ensure that the process is effective but does not create a bottleneck in the recruitment process?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think in the interest of time, I will keep it short.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: We would be able to automate these processes so that the processing times will not be lengthened.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Earlier on, in my main speech, I have also shared that there will be a rubric that published on our website.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Companies, before they even apply, they can actually score the potential candidate on the rubric.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: And they will also know before they even apply, what is the chance of this EP being approved.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Most of the businesses that we have spoken to, that we have gotten feedback from, appreciate the transparency, the clarity that COMPASS brings.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think this is a very important feature for us in designing and implementing COMPASS.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: COMPASS is meant to tell the world we are open, we are connected and we are welcoming of foreign work pass holders to come in and work as long as they can help uplift our economy, contribute to our workforce in uplifting and strengthening the Singaporean Core.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Desmond Choo, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
text: The debate is not over when there are still questions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Minister Tan See Leng, Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad and Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon and Minister of State Gan Siow Huang for their indulgence in their clarifications in preparing for this Committee of Supply.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: I also want to congratulate them for taking very bold but measured steps to build workers' compact but at the same time, keeping the workforce competitive.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: We know that it is a difficult policy tightrope for them to walk and they can be reassured of the tripartite support to their efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: At the same time, I also want to thank Permanent Secretary Aubeck Kam and his team.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: He has done quite a fair bit to strengthen tripartite relations and we want to extend our appreciation for his efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Choo
text: With this, Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
